_comment: Copy to .claude/gates.json and replace with commands that actually pass today. fast = every edit; full = before any 'done' claim; deferred = CI only.

fast.name: unit
fast.cmd: echo 'TODO: your fast unit test command'

deferred: _comment_test_delta: reporting tier ON PURPOSE, not an oversight. Requiring tests does not improve correctness on current models (arXiv:2602.07900: GPT-5.2 writes tests in 0.6% of tasks and resolves 71.8%; Claude Opus 4.5 writes them in 83% and resolves 74.4%; forcing via prompt gives p>0.05). Its value is regression insurance over time, which nobody has measured. Promote it to 'full' deliberately if that bet is one you want to make. See docs/04-gate-ladder.md 2.3.

_comment_holdout: needs HOLDOUT_DIR pointing OUTSIDE the repo. Isolation, not secrecy, is the property that matters — a red team scored 100% on SWE-bench Verified and Pro via a conftest.py hook without solving anything. Reports the visible-vs-held-out gap; no threshold.

_comment_mutate: diff-scoped, <=1 mutant per line, dismissible via a Mutation-Dismissed commit trailer. No score threshold on purpose — Google runs this across >24,000 developers without one, and unfiltered mutants were rated 85% unproductive.
